Oceania Train Guide

Australia and New Zealand run almost no fast trains and several of the world's great slow ones — the Ghan up the middle of the continent, the Indian Pacific across the Nullarbor, and the TranzAlpine over the Southern Alps. This is who operates each of them, where they go, and an honest read on which are worth taking as journeys and which are simply the way to reach the Blue Mountains. Transcontinental Journeys

The long-distance services that cross Australia end to end

The Ghan
JOURNEY BEYOND · Adelaide to Darwin
Scenic
Origin / Hub
🇦🇺 Australia
↔
Key Routes
Adelaide ↔ Alice Springs ↔ Darwin (~54h, 2 nights)
Off-train excursions at Alice Springs and Katherine included
What it is like

Three thousand kilometres up the centre of Australia, and the emptiness is the attraction — this is a train for people who want to watch nothing happen beautifully for two days. Fares are all-inclusive of meals, drinks and the off-train excursions, which is why the headline price looks steep. Gold Twin cabins are snug with bunks; Platinum buys a proper double and a lot of money. Not transport, and priced accordingly.

Indian Pacific
JOURNEY BEYOND · Sydney to Perth
Scenic
Origin / Hub
🇦🇺 Australia
↔
Key Routes
Sydney ↔ Broken Hill ↔ Adelaide ↔ Perth (~65h, 3 nights)
Includes the Nullarbor's 478 km dead-straight section
What it is like

Ocean to ocean across the continent, including the longest straight stretch of railway track in the world — which is exactly as hypnotic and as monotonous as it sounds. Three nights is a lot of Nullarbor, and this is the one where the shorter Adelaide–Perth leg is a legitimate way to get most of the drama for less time and money. Same all-inclusive model and same cabin grades as the Ghan.

NSW TrainLink XPT & Intercity
TRANSPORT FOR NSW
Intercity
Origin / Hub
🇦🇺 Australia
↔
Key Routes
Sydney ↔ Melbourne (XPT, ~11h)
Sydney ↔ Brisbane (XPT, ~14h, incl. overnight)
Sydney ↔ Katoomba, Blue Mountains (~2h)
Sydney ↔ Canberra (~4h 20m)
What it is like

The Blue Mountains line is the one to actually use — a two-hour double-decker run from Central to Katoomba on an Opal card, and far better than driving up on a weekend. The long-haul XPT to Melbourne is a different matter: eleven hours against a ninety-minute flight, on 1980s stock. Take it if you like trains or dislike flying; nobody takes it to save time. Sleeper berths on the Brisbane service are basic but do the job.

Spirit of Queensland & Kuranda Scenic Railway
QUEENSLAND RAIL
Intercity
Origin / Hub
🇦🇺 Australia
↔
Key Routes
Brisbane ↔ Townsville ↔ Cairns (~25h, tilt train)
Cairns ↔ Kuranda (~2h, Barron Gorge)
What it is like

The Spirit of Queensland's RailBed seats lie fully flat and are the only proper business-class-style beds on Australian rail, which makes a long coastal run genuinely restful. Kuranda is the famous one: a two-hour climb past Barron Falls through fifteen tunnels, usually paired with the Skyrail gondola for the return so you see the rainforest from both angles. Book Kuranda ahead in dry season — it fills with day trippers from Cairns.

V/Line
VICTORIA · regional network from Melbourne
Regional
Origin / Hub
🇦🇺 Australia
↔
Key Routes
Melbourne ↔ Geelong (~1h)
Melbourne ↔ Ballarat / Bendigo (~1h 30m)
Melbourne ↔ Warrnambool (for the Great Ocean Road's western end)
What it is like

Ordinary regional trains that happen to be extraordinarily cheap — Victoria capped regional fares in 2023, so a two-hour run to Bendigo costs about the same as a city tram ride. That makes the goldfields towns and Geelong easy days out without a car. It does not reach the Great Ocean Road itself; the train gets you to Geelong or Warrnambool and a bus or hire car does the rest.

TranzAlpine
GREAT JOURNEYS NZ (KIWIRAIL)
Scenic
Origin / Hub
🇳🇿 New Zealand
↔
Key Routes
Christchurch ↔ Arthur's Pass ↔ Greymouth (~5h)
What it is like

Five hours across the Southern Alps — braided rivers, beech forest, and a viaduct-and-tunnel climb to Arthur's Pass — and it deserves its reputation as one of the world's great rail journeys. The open-air viewing carriage is where to spend the mountain sections, and it is cold; take a jacket even in summer. Most people ride out and back in a day, which works, though Arthur's Pass makes a better stop than Greymouth.

Coastal Pacific & Northern Explorer
GREAT JOURNEYS NZ (KIWIRAIL)
Scenic
Origin / Hub
🇳🇿 New Zealand
↔
Key Routes
Christchurch ↔ Kaikōura ↔ Picton (Coastal Pacific, ~6h)
Auckland ↔ Tongariro ↔ Wellington (Northern Explorer, ~11h)
What it is like

The Coastal Pacific runs between the Pacific and the Kaikōura ranges with seals on the rocks below, and it connects with the Interislander ferry at Picton, which makes it a genuinely practical link between the islands. The Northern Explorer crosses the volcanic plateau and the Raurimu Spiral but has long dull stretches either side. Both are seasonal or reduced in winter — check before building a route around them.
